label: rem:fundamental-object-remark
title: The fundamental object under a fibre functor
html:
The volume form \epsilon of a fundamental object, with its coform \eta, exhibits V as its own dual: a symplectic self-dual object, the datum that distinguishes \mathrm{SL}_2 / \mathrm{SU}(2) from \mathrm{GL}_2 [deligne1990].

Under a fibre functor the volume constraint forces \mathrm{rank}(V) = 2, so V is simple of categorical dimension 2: in \mathrm{SU}(2) it is V = V_{1/2} \cong \mathbb{C}^2, every other simple object is an exterior or symmetric power of V, and V tensor-generates \mathbf{C} (the role of V is spelled out in a remark below).
